question.text: If \(a > 0, a \in R, z=a+2 i\) and \(z|z|-a z+1=0\) then

options.text: \(z\) is always a positive real number
\(z\) is always a negative real number
such a complex z does not exist

solution.text: Putting \(z=a+2 i\) in the given equation and comparing imaginary parts, we get \(\mathrm{a}^2+4=\mathrm{a}^2\), which is not possible.
